At the end of all the Defence cases, will we have one videolink for witnesses for whom affidavits were used and for which the Chamber rules that they should be cross-examined by video in the order of the indictment or will we organise a videolink for each of the Defence cases separately? If we were to do it for each Defence case, then the rhythm and timetable of the hearings might be upset, because I wish to draw the attention of the Chamber that we will use our two weeks for the presentation of evidence here in court, and what the Prosecution is requesting, and if this request is granted, that is, the cross-examination of my experts in my case or affidavit witnesses, I have no intention of spending my time for the benefit of the Prosecution. So the Chamber will have to find some additional time to meet the requests of Ms. Somers. So I would request that a decision be made about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Fila. As always, you have raised a good point. I had it in mind myself, exactly to see how we're going to proceed. It's one thing to send a team to hear two witnesses, for instance, have them brought back, and then again send the same team back again to hear one witness, then they come back, et cetera, et cetera. So the question does indeed arise whether we could not perhaps see, and I was going to suggest that we wait until we hear the Prosecutor tell us, "I wish to cross-examine such-and-such witness," and once we know the position of the Prosecution, then we would know whose affidavits have not been accepted, and they need to be cross-examined, how many such persons there are, and then we can discuss amongst ourselves to see whether we agree to move for one week, for two days or three days, or for one day to hear all the people over there at once, to do it at the same time instead of the other way. So I think that we have to think about this, but perhaps it is too early. But still it is important to have all that information. Otherwise, it could be too late. I would like to ask the Prosecution to make an extra effort to tell us what their position is in relation to all the affidavits so that we might organise ourselves. As I have said, I have asked the Defence to do everything in their power for the important witnesses to come here to the courtroom. I know it's difficult to make the decision, because, after all, all witnesses are important, but those that the Defence wish to call here, that they should do so. As for the others, that we should use affidavits. This was more or less a directive of the Chamber. Now I'm asking the Prosecution. Tell us, with a maximum degree of optimism, how we can facilitate things, because as I have already said, we have to complete this case, so facilitate things, of course, without prejudice to justice. If you have serious reasons for cross-examining, tell us, or if you can facilitate things, tell us that too so we can organise ourselves. As soon as we have your reply, we can have a Status Conference to discuss all these matters. Ms. Susan Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could in the next day or so, in the next day, give a summary to the Chamber and copies to counsel as to exactly what we have in the way of affidavits, because the two Kvocka ones are the subject of today's response, and I tried to get it in earlier than it was due so that you'd have that. So it will be in today. We have the Prcac affidavits and a very large binder from the Radic team was presented which we have not gone through. I don't know whether it contains the affidavits or not. So that's -- if they're in there, we can certainly assess as quickly as possible on those. What I might suggest, if the Chamber is so inclined, I agree with counsel that to go for two people is completely not feasible. However, if there is a larger number of videolink witnesses with another accused's set of witnesses, we would not oppose -- I don't think it would have any negative impact because you've heard the testimony any way. I think it would be no problem to tack on those as well. We want to do it quickly and not -- and with the most economical approach. So we will certainly have maximum give on any of those issues. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I make a brief comment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, do, Mr. Simic. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] I am afraid that the approach of my learned friends from the Prosecution derogates the very meaning of affidavits. An affidavit is not an ordinary statement. It is a statement which can be interpreted and judged only in the context of the witness' testimony which it is corroborating. And that is why I did not give my affidavits to Ms. Somers. Only two affidavits linked to these two testimonies. Tomorrow I will file a submission with the other affidavits. And if the Prosecution feels that it is necessary to cross-examine even before hearing the witness' testimony, then the very meaning of the Rule, whose intention is to expedite proceedings, will be lost because these affidavits corroborate witness' testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you, Mr. Simic. We would like to ask the Prosecutor, when they tell us that they want to cross-examine, to give us the reasons. Of course, there's no need to tell you that because you know that that comes within the discretionary powers of the Chamber which it may use. So if you tell us you wish to cross-examine "because," then we are in a position to decide. And that is the approach we will take. So we will see whether the Chamber will authorise cross-examination, and we will see -- we will make a decision if we consider the reasons given are valid. Ms. Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour. We have put in -- we've tried to keep it a very short response, and it gives the ground. We realise we are in the Chamber's hands with this, but our objections, more often than not, go to the fact that it would be an inappropriate witness because the matter would go to a core issue. And we are trying to find those where it would not be in issue. So far, they have not come across our desk. But, of course, we realise that. We do have only the 65 ter summary to go on. So looking at that, which is not terribly meaty, we look at the affidavit which may be, before the witness testifies, heartier than what we know about the witness, and we try to make our judgements at that time. As I indicated, the witnesses have just finished, and we try to get these responses in before the seven days have elapsed. We think it's important that you have it. So based on what limited knowledge I am given about the summary, and then looking at the more weighty matter that's provided, not weighty in the sense of value but volume, I am trying to make a judgement on rather limited facts. But we will nonetheless do it. We do want to see it move.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You asked, Ms. Somers, whether we were having hearings next week. The answer is no. I remain optimistic in hoping that you will have enough time to do your work so that we will be able to move forward a little more quickly, and I thank Mr. Simic for having conducted things as he has done and to make even greater improvements the next time, if possible. So I wish you success in your work. Until -- I don't have the calendar. You know the date when we will be resuming the hearings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
